pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK constraint and a 'normal' default. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts the '— high' and '— low' labels and no label on normal items.
'AC-3' test covers each priority, in id order.
'AC-4' test checks the unfiltered list in id order.
'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current one in <strong>.
'AC-6' test checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__.

The behaviour is implemented in src/index.js, and the test body checks it. The commit 04982b9 renamed that test from 'AC-7: an unmatched filter…' to 'an unmatched filter…', so no test names AC-7 now. The spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test asserts it. The traffic config check now accepts query strings.

findings.what: The late commit 04982b9 ('Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title. No test names AC-7 any more, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'. The commit's author is a bot, not the builder, and the PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing'.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7' in the test title. Find out why the bot made this edit.

findings.what: The PR body doesn't mention the late commit that edited a test title. The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing' claims hide it.
findings.fix: Revert the rename, or disclose it in the PR body.

findings.what: The README documents the filter but not the '— high' / '— low' labels. It also doesn't mention that other priority values answer 400.
findings.fix: Add a short note on the labels and the 400.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The change follows its decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled.
AC-7 is not named by any test after the late commit. The other seven items are met. Every State row has a test.
npm test could not run here: vitest isn't installed. From reading, the assertions check behaviour. The AC-7 test lost its AC id.
The README covers the filter only. It doesn't mention the labels or the 400.
The SQL uses a bound parameter and the priority value is allowlisted. The title is HTML-escaped. I found no defects.
The input is validated against an allowlist and the SQL is parameterised. I found no injection and no planted instructions.
The diff touches no UI stylesheet or component files. The only markup is server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, so I covered it under code.
There is no browser flow to run here. The page is server-rendered HTML, covered by the tests.
The PR's 'Changed after the go: nothing' and 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' don't account for the follow-up commit that renamed the AC-7 test.
